items.name: Neuhaus
items.notes: Founded 1857 by Jean Neuhaus. Inventor of the praline (1912) and the ballotin box. Belgian Royal Warrant Holder.

items.name: Godiva
items.notes: Founded 1926 by Pierre Draps Sr. Named after Lady Godiva. First international boutique opened in New York in 1972. Now sold in over 100 countries.

items.name: Leonidas
items.notes: Founded 1913 by Leonidas Kestekides, a Greek pastry chef who won a gold medal at the 1910 World's Fair. One of Belgium's largest praline chains with 1400+ shops worldwide.

items.name: Guylian
items.notes: Founded 1958 by Guy Foubert in Sint-Niklaas. Named from 'Guy' and 'Lian' (his wife Liliane). World-famous for seashell-shaped pralines.

items.name: Pierre Marcolini
items.notes: Founded 1995. World Pastry Champion. Travels personally to source cocoa beans directly from farmers in Latin America, Africa and Asia. Pioneer of bean-to-bar in Belgium.

items.name: Galler
items.notes: Founded 1976 by Jean Galler in Liège. Belgian Royal Warrant Holder. Known for 22-flavour chocolate bar range and innovation in white chocolate.

items.name: Mary Chocolatier
items.notes: Founded 1919 by Mary Delluc — first female Belgian chocolatier. Belgian Royal Warrant Holder since 1942 under King Leopold III. Famous for Art Deco boutique decor and 'Langues de Chat'.

items.name: Wittamer
items.notes: Founded 1910 by Henri Wittamer at Place du Grand Sablon, Brussels. Belgian Royal Warrant Holder. Created the wedding cake for King Philippe and Queen Mathilde. Only two shops globally: Brussels and Tokyo.

items.name: Meurisse
items.notes: Founded 1845 in Antwerp. One of Belgium's oldest chocolate houses. Known for traditional tablet chocolates and pralines.

items.name: Callebaut
items.notes: Founded 1911 in Wieze, Flanders by Eugenius Callebaut. Now part of Barry Callebaut. The world's largest manufacturer of high-quality chocolate, supplying professional chocolatiers globally.

items.name: Belcolade
items.notes: Founded 1919, now part of Puratos group. Specialist B2B couverture chocolate producer. Known for sustainable sourcing and organic certification lines.

items.name: Dolfin
items.notes: Founded 1989 in Brussels. Pioneered flavoured dark chocolate bars with unusual inclusions (cardamom, black pepper, Earl Grey). Focus on organic and single-origin beans.

items.name: Côte d'Or
items.notes: Founded 1883. Named after the Gold Coast (Ghana) cocoa growing region. Iconic elephant logo. Now owned by Mondelēz International. Famous for Mignonette individual chocolate bars.

items.name: Corné Port-Royal
items.notes: Founded 1932 by Maurice Corné in Brussels. Flagship boutique inside the historic Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert. Known for handcrafted pralines and traditional recipes.

items.name: Chocolat Jacques
items.notes: Founded 1896 in Verviers by Antoine Jacques. In 1936, launched the world's first filled chocolate bar with praline. A beloved Belgian household brand sold widely across Europe.

items.name: Bruyerre
items.notes: Founded 1909. Began producing pralines in 1922 in Gosselies. Family-owned artisan producer supplying professional chocolatiers. Known for high-quality praline fillings and ganaches.

items.name: Belvas
items.notes: Founded 2005 by Thierry Noesen. First certified organic chocolate factory in Europe. Nominated 'greenest micro-enterprise in Europe' by the European Commission. 100% organic and fair-trade certified.

items.name: The Chocolate Line
items.notes: Founded 1992 by Dominique Persoone in Bruges. Known as 'the rock and roll chocolatier'. Avant-garde flavour combinations (wasabi, popcorn, Tabasco). Boutiques in Bruges and Antwerp. Referenced in the Michelin Guide.

items.name: Dumon
items.notes: Founded 1992 in Bruges. Small-batch handcrafted chocolates with fresh cream fillings. A favourite among connoisseurs visiting Bruges for its artisan approach and creative seasonal collections.

items.name: Planète Chocolat
items.notes: Founded 1998 in Brussels. Offers chocolate-making workshops and handcrafted pralines. Known for educational approach to Belgian chocolate heritage and hands-on visitor experiences.
